lines.text: Premarital screening protects the next marriage.
Silsila protects the marriages that already happened.
When a newborn screen finds a recessive condition, the baby's relatives are far more likely to be carriers. Where cousins marry, many of them are already married to each other. And no one tells them.
In the only national survey, half of Emirati marriages were between relatives.
When the extended families of affected children were tested, 31% of relatives were carriers, and in 8% of married couples, both were.
lines.say: When the extended families of affected children were tested, 31 percent of relatives were carriers, and in 8 percent of married couples, both were.

lines.text: Abu Dhabi's programmes already find the first person: 565 incompatible couples in premarital testing, and more than 100 babies through newborn screening in the past year. The country has nine practising genetic counsellors.

Silsila is the step after the result. An exact engine works out every relative's chance. The family decides who is told. A genetic counsellor approves every invitation. And each case closes only with evidence.
This is the live product, running in the UAE, with a fictional family. Baby Zayed's newborn screen finds congenital adrenal hyperplasia. His parents are first cousins.
Silsila calculates every relative's chance exactly, across both cousin marriages, and ranks whom to tell first: his aunt Noura, who is pregnant.
His mother, Mariam, gives permission and chooses an anonymous invitation: no name, no condition. Nothing is sent until a counsellor approves it.
Noura opens a private link, in Arabic or English. Every sentence is approved wording, or a word-for-word quotation from MedlinePlus, and it can be read aloud.
She passes a comprehension check, reads her options in the source's own words, described and never recommended, and books counselling.
When she asks whether to end the pregnancy, Silsila does not answer. A counsellor is alerted. Her test result then closes the case, with evidence.
No language model writes anything a family reads. When a model tries, the output gate blocks it.
Every action is written to an audit log, each entry chained to the last by its hash. In 10,000 unauthorised requests, there were zero disclosures.
lines.say: Every action is written to an audit log, each entry chained to the last by its hash. In ten thousand unauthorised requests, there were zero disclosures.

lines.text: And the programme sees comprehension, uptake and time to counselling. It never counts marriages or reproductive choices.
This is the Family Twin: a simulated clan of 61 people, with six cousin marriages. Record one result, and every relative's chance is recalculated exactly, in about a second.
The engine agrees with an independent solver on 30,000 of 30,000 probabilities.
lines.say: The engine agrees with an independent solver on thirty thousand of thirty thousand probabilities.

lines.text: And across many simulated clans, inviting relatives in Silsila's order found 1.58 times as many at-risk couples per test as an unranked cascade.
Why not let a language model do it? We measured the co-creators' own models, pre-registered, on 150 families. In free text, Jais 3 7B gave an exact number in 59.4% of its answers.
lines.say: Why not let a language model do it? We measured the co-creators' own models, pre-registered, on 150 families. In free text, Jais 3, seven B, gave an exact number in 59.4 percent of its answers.

lines.text: So models do one job here. A family tells its story in Emirati Arabic, Jais drafts the family tree, and a counsellor confirms every person before the engine runs.
Even the guide that answers questions about Silsila uses no AI: fixed answers, and live lookups you can check.
The first result arrives as a FHIR record, and is refused if it is preliminary or uncertain.
lines.say: The first result arrives as a fire record, and is refused if it is preliminary or uncertain.

lines.text: It is deployed today in the UAE, on ordinary processors, with no model at run time. It works in Arabic and English, with zero accessibility violations on every screen.

The buyer already produces the index results, and counsellor time is the scarce resource. As a projection: 100 index newborns a year means about 25 at-risk couples found for this condition, against 17 without ranking.
The proposal is a pilot at one screening centre: first in shadow mode beside counsellors, then with counsellor-approved invitations, and every measure reported to the Department of Health.
Six criteria, and for each one, something you can open and a number you can check.
What is not yet shown, said plainly: no patient has used it. The evidence is on simulated families. Three genes. And the Arabic awaits a native clinical review.
Silsila. The step after the result.
